name: Kakwa
region: West Nile, Uganda (Koboko, Yumbe), Central Equatoria in South Sudan and Aru in DR Congo
translator_note: Drafted in everyday Koboko Kakwa addressed to one person (do), leaning on the Bari-group core Kakwa shares with Bari and Kuku (nan, do, yi; tu, po, met, dendya, kondya, tindya; ngutu, kadi, kolong, kutuk) and on the loans Koboko speech already carries from Swahili, Arabic and English (motoka, safari, simu, sente, bei, boma, siteji, kodi, app, link, sandbox, plug-in). Buttons are bare verbs: Tu (go), Kapa (share), Kodi (rent), Yoo (send), 'Du UG (book on UG). The implosive apostrophe follows the standard orthography ('bu, 'dit, 'dini). No native reviewer has read this and Kakwa was the thinnest of the five sources: the verbs for book, choose, keep, forget and accept, the negation, and the tense particle a are the weakest points, and every paragraph is a close paraphrase that a Koboko speaker should expect to rewrite.
